Repairs are in. All three listed sheet failures came from figure-spec text that the renderer could not satisfy, so I fixed the specs rather than the invention text.

**FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 (hatching):** both briefs prescribed hatch angles and comparative steepness ("legs rising to the right", "band falling to the right more steeply than the slab", the FIG. 4 stack of three differently sloped bands). The renderer applies one hatch angle, so every comparative and directional statement was a guaranteed mismatch on inspection. Hatch slope is not disclosure-grounded geometry, so I removed the angle and direction prescriptions and kept the thing that actually separates the bodies: regularly spaced parallel hatching on each cut body with a plain solid line along every join. FIG. 4's cross-references to FIG. 2's hatch direction went with them.

**FIG. 5 (numeral 24):** numeral 24 kept landing in a rejected coordinate cluster on the narrow front strip of the band. The perimeter member is already fully identified on FIG. 1, FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, and FIG. 5 exists to show the flexible pulling element, so I removed numeral 24 and the canonical part name from that sheet and left the structure as an unnumbered band under the body, as context only. FIG. 5 now carries 10, 36, 46. The Brief Description of the Drawings entry for FIG. 5 was updated to match.

I edited the figure specifications and the drawings section; I did not run the image pipeline or the gates myself, so the regeneration and re-inspection happen on this turn's publish, not in anything I verified here.

input.summary: Resolved all three drawing-gate blockers from the previous QA report by correcting figure specifications, with one consequential synchronization in the Brief Description of the Drawings. FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 failed semantic review because their briefs prescribed hatching directions and comparative steepness between adjacent cut bodies that the renderer does not vary; those prescriptions are drawing convention, not disclosure-grounded geometry, so they were removed and replaced with the positive statement that each cut body carries regularly spaced parallel hatching and that a plain solid line runs along every join. FIG. 5 failed leader placement on numeral 24, which repeatedly landed in a rejected coordinate cluster on the narrow front strip of the band; since the perimeter member is fully identified on FIG. 1, FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, numeral 24 and the canonical part name were removed from FIG. 5 and the structure left as an unnumbered band shown only as context, and the FIG. 5 sentence in the drawings section was updated accordingly. No claim, no numeral definition, and no technical statement in the specification was changed. Note on verification: the figure specifications were edited here, but the image regeneration and the geometry, leader, OCR and visual gates run in the publish pipeline, not in this session, so I have not personally observed those checks pass.
reasoning: The FIG. 2 failures were all of one kind: the brief asserted relative hatch slopes (legs rising to the right, covering element steeper than the base) that the renderer cannot honour because it applies a single hatch pattern. Any comparative or directional hatch statement in these briefs is therefore a standing semantic-review failure. Hatch angle is a depiction convention with no support in the inventor source, so the correct repair is to delete the unsatisfiable constraint rather than to keep regenerating against it.

Body separation still has to read in a sectional view, so I kept the positive, renderable requirement that carries that work: each cut body filled with regularly spaced parallel hatching, and a plain solid line along each join so adjacent bodies do not merge. This is stated affirmatively rather than as a ban on linework.

FIG. 4 carried the same defect twice, once in the three-band stack and once in the column, and both statements cross-referenced FIG. 2's hatch direction. Removing the direction language from FIG. 2 without removing those cross-references would have left the brief internally inconsistent, so both were cut in the same pass.

For FIG. 5 the leader failure was positional, not descriptive: numeral 24 targeted the front strip of a band drawn under the rectangular body, and the endpoint inspection rejected the cluster. Rather than tightening the target with an aesthetic coordinate constraint, which the drafting rules forbid, I removed the numeral from the sheet. The perimeter member remains numbered on four other sheets including the enlarged section that is dedicated to its lower end, so nothing about the disclosure becomes unillustrated.

Having removed numeral 24 from FIG. 5, the rules require that its canonical part name go too, so the band is now described only as a band running round the underside of the body, an unnumbered context shape. I checked that the detailed description does not state that the perimeter member is visible in FIG. 5; it does not, so only the Brief Description of the Drawings sentence needed the matching edit.

I deliberately left everything else alone. The review listed no text, source-fidelity, numeral-table or claim defect, and the numeral table remains correct because 24 is still used, still defined once, and still appears on sheets that list it.

figures/FIG-4-ENLARGED-SECTION-OF-THE-PERIMETER-MEMBER-END.md: removed the hatch direction and relative steepness assigned to the covering element, the bonding material and the substrate, and removed the perimeter member column's hatch direction and its cross-reference to FIG. 2, leaving regularly spaced parallel hatching on the column.

figures/FIG-5-SECOND-EMBODIMENT-WITH-A-PULLING-ELEMENT.md: deleted the perimeter member 24 identification bullet and removed 24 from both numeral lists, which now read 10, 36, 46; the band under the body remains as an unnumbered context shape with no canonical part name.
draft/07-drawings.md: removed the perimeter member from the list of parts shown schematically in FIG. 5, so the brief description matches the sheet.
